rows.name: Evidence pages cited in investor dossiers
rows.publisher: various (investor websites, press releases, news, registers)
rows.licence: varies per page; stored for verification only, quoted under short-quotation rules
rows.coverage_estimate: every URL in core.evidence
rows.limitations: JavaScript-only pages and paywalls cannot be verified by script
rows.notes: Pseudo-source so that evidence re-fetches are logged in meta.fetch_run like every other source.

rows.name: SEC Form D data sets (Regulation D offering notices)
rows.licence: US government public data, free to access; no explicit reuse licence found (US federal works generally public domain [unverified]); EDGAR fair-access rules apply
rows.update_cadence: Quarterly ZIPs (latest 2026 Q3, page updated 30 Sep 2026); XML submissions from Jan 2008
rows.coverage_estimate: All Reg D notice filers: 34,553 new Reg D offerings in 2025 (32,554 in 2024) [secondary, citing SEC DERA]; pooled funds took ~89% of the $2.39tn raised but are a little under half of offerings, implying ~15-17k new pooled-fund Form Ds a year [estimate]; Sep 2026: 277 new venture fund vehicles from 196 sponsors [vendor tracker] (as of 2026-10-25)
rows.limitations: Data 'as filed', accuracy not guaranteed by the SEC. TOTALAMOUNTSOLD goes stale because many funds never amend. Non-US funds, 4(a)(2) deals and non-filers are missing. MINIMUMINVESTMENTACCEPTED is the LP minimum, not the fund's ticket, so no ticket size. Operating-company filings do not name investors (RELATEDPERSONS = officers, directors, promoters). Filed per vehicle (SPVs, feeders), so dedupe to sponsor. Attachments excluded. Published counts conflict; recompute fund counts from raw data.
rows.notes: Six tab-delimited UTF-8 tables (FORMDSUBMISSION, ISSUERS, OFFERING, RECIPIENTS, RELATEDPERSONS, SIGNATURES) keyed on ACCESSIONNUMBER, ~3.5 MB per quarter. For a fund, TOTALOFFERINGAMOUNT = target size and TOTALAMOUNTSOLD = raised so far; the filing date is dated proof of fundraising. Filter INDUSTRYGROUPTYPE='Pooled Investment Fund' and ISAMENDMENT=false, group by INVESTMENTFUNDTYPE. Join to Form ADV via the Form D file number (021-...) and to EDGAR submissions via issuer CIK.

rows.name: SEC Form ADV and IAPD (incl. Schedule D 7.B.(1) private fund reporting)
rows.licence: US government public data, free to access; no explicit reuse licence found
rows.update_cadence: Monthly RIA and ERA report files (latest Oct 2026); filings annual plus amendments; full Part 1 bulk CSV covers 19 Oct 2000 - 31 Dec 2024, later data via IAPD
rows.coverage_estimate: 16,544 SEC-registered advisers (2025 data) [secondary, trade association]; ERAs: 5,390 filing with the SEC and ~3,920-3,940 with states (2023 data, sources differ) [pre-2024]; 4,117 VC funds in Schedule D data for H1 2025 [secondary]; Form PF lists only 362 VC advisers vs ~2,984 US VC firms (2025), so ADV, which ERAs also file, is the better US VC backbone (as of 2026-10-25)
rows.limitations: Self-reported. Q11 gross asset value is annual, gross and excludes uncalled commitments. ERAs file only Items 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 10 and 11 (no Item 5 regulatory AUM), so ERA AUM must be summed from 7.B.(1). No sector or ticket size (Part 2A brochures, RIAs only, give strategy text). Fund names may be coded (rule 204-2(d)). Monthly report files hold a subset of items and do not mention Schedule D; the format of 2025+ data on IAPD (adviserinfo.sec.gov/adv) and whether 7.B.(1) is a separate table are unconfirmed. Form PF data is not on IAPD.
rows.notes: Schedule D 7.B.(1) per private fund: name and private fund ID (805-...), jurisdiction, GP/manager, 3(c)(1)/3(c)(7), fund-of-funds flag, fund type (incl. venture capital and private equity), current gross asset value, LP minimum commitment, number of beneficial owners, Form D file number (021-...). Item 2.B ERA exemption 'solely to one or more venture capital funds' (rule 203(l)-1) is a strong VC flag. Part 2 brochures and Form CRS are separate PDF ZIPs.

rows.name: SEC Private Fund Statistics (Form PF aggregates)
rows.licence: US government public data, free to access; no explicit reuse licence found
rows.coverage_estimate: 58,891 private funds in 2025Q4 (27,682 PE, 4,392 VC), $29.6tn gross / $19.0tn net assets; 4,153 advisers reporting (2,047 PE, 362 VC), i.e. roughly 12% of ~2,984 US VC firms (as of 19 Aug 2026)
rows.limitations: Aggregate only: no per-fund or per-adviser public data, and Form PF data will not be published on IAPD. Only SEC-registered advisers with at least $150m private fund AUM file, so most VC managers (ERAs) are missing. Advisers are counted for three quarters after each quarter they report.
rows.notes: Benchmark only, e.g. for checking Form ADV / Form D load coverage. Fund and adviser counts by type are in a downloadable JSON file. ~13.5 PE funds per PE adviser, so records must be deduped to the manager level.

rows.name: SEC Form 13F data sets and Schedules 13D/G
rows.licence: US government public data, free to access; no explicit reuse licence found
rows.update_cadence: 13F data sets quarterly (latest Jun-Aug 2026, page updated 31 Aug 2026); 13D/G event-driven
rows.coverage_estimate: 13F data sets from July 2013 to Jun-Aug 2026; filer counts not checked (as of 2026-10-25)
rows.limitations: Listed (13(f)) securities only; says nothing about private holdings. Filing thresholds (13F at least $100m in 13(f) securities; 13D/G above 5% stakes) unverified. Private-market activity of the family offices found still needs press or Form D evidence.
rows.notes: Identifies large US family offices and crossover funds with a dated public filing. Since March 2024 each 13F set covers the three months ending Feb, May, Aug or Nov; data is flattened 'as filed' XML.

rows.name: SEC Crowdfunding Offerings Data Sets (Regulation CF, Form C)
rows.licence: US government public data, free to access; no explicit reuse licence found
rows.coverage_estimate: Quarterly data sets 2016 Q2 - 2026 Q3 from Form C, C-U, annual reports and terminations; co-issuer data from 2021Q1 (as of 2026-10-25)
rows.limitations: No investor identities: covers issuers and funding portals only. SEC does not guarantee accuracy. Field detail (target and maximum amounts, progress updates) unverified.
rows.notes: Useful only for the crowdfunding-platform investor type, not for identifying angels.

rows.name: SEC EDGAR APIs, bulk indexes and Full-Text Search
rows.licence: Free to access ('anyone can access and download this information for free'); fair-access rules: max 10 requests/second, declared User-Agent, no botnets or automated crawling
rows.update_cadence: submissions.zip and companyfacts.zip rebuilt nightly (~03:00 ET); daily and full indexes
rows.coverage_estimate: All EDGAR filers; Full-Text Search covers filings since 2001 including attachments (as of 2026-10-25)
rows.limitations: No authentication but no CORS; no SEC technical support; rate cap may be lowered. Full-Text Search is a web interface only; its JSON endpoint (efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index) is undocumented and reportedly capped at 10,000 hits per query [secondary]. XBRL endpoints cover 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, 20-F, 40-F and 6-K only.
rows.notes: Plumbing for the Form D, ADV and 13F loaders: nightly submissions.zip as filing-history index (join on issuer CIK), full-index files for accession lists, Feed/Oldloads archives and CIK/ticker files. Keep a <=10 req/s token bucket with a contact User-Agent; do not use Full-Text Search as a bulk source.

rows.name: Companies House (Free Company Data Product, PSC snapshot, API)
rows.licence: Free; reuse licence (often described as the Open Government Licence) not confirmed on the pages fetched; bulk product 'provided free of charge and will not be supported'
rows.update_cadence: Company data monthly (to previous month-end, published within 5 working days; latest 2026-10-01, 471 MB); PSC snapshot daily (latest 2026-10-25, ~2.4 GB); API live
rows.coverage_estimate: All UK companies; 4,377 active companies with SIC 64303 'venture and development capital' (Dec 2025) [secondary]
rows.limitations: SIC codes are self-chosen and noisy: SIC 64303 mostly catches SPVs, holding and personal investment companies, so it is a candidate list, not proof of investing. PSC only shows control of 25% or more, so minority VC stakes are missed. Shareholders appear only in confirmation statements and SH01 filings (PDF, needs OCR; no bulk structured shareholder dataset [unverified]). API limit 600 requests per 5 minutes (429 on breach; repeat abusers may be banned).
rows.notes: Use the monthly and daily bulk files for the base load and the API for deltas (~172,800 calls/day max). Candidate SIC codes 64303, 64209, 64999, 66300 [descriptions unverified]. Reverse PSC lookup of known fund GPs/LPs as controllers of operating companies gives dated, mainly PE/buyout, investment evidence. Require proof from another source (FCA, Form D/ADV, LP disclosure, portfolio page).

rows.name: FCA Financial Services Register and register of small registered UK AIFMs
rows.licence: API terms of use not found (registration and key required)
rows.coverage_estimate: 2,721 FCA-authorised AIFMs (1 Sep 2017) and 105 firms with only the small-AIFM requirement (Feb 2021) [pre-2024]; current counts not determined (as of 2026-10-25)
rows.limitations: No documented bulk download. Rate limit ~50 requests per 10 s with a 1-minute block on breach per a third-party client (another source says 100 per 60 s); official terms not read. Small-AIFM list includes lapsed firms, so it is not an active count. Confirms regulatory status only, not AUM or deployment.
rows.notes: GET-only REST API (base https://register.fca.org.uk/services/V0.1) with X-AUTH-EMAIL and X-AUTH-KEY headers; endpoints Firm (FRN: permissions, passports, individuals, appointed representatives, disciplinary history), Individuals (IRN), Funds/CIS (PRN) and Search. Relevant permissions: managing an AIF, small registered AIFM, RVECA/SEF manager. Script FRN lookups seeded from Companies House, ESMA or GLEIF names. Small registered AIFM annual fee £781.

rows.name: British Business Bank / British Patient Capital results
rows.coverage_estimate: 44 fund managers and ~1,350 underlying companies; £2,287m since inception across 80 fund commitments, 10 co-investments and 18 Future Fund: Breakthrough deals (year to 31 Mar 2024); 70 funds by 40 firms (Mar 2023) [pre-2024]
rows.limitations: Aggregate totals in press releases only; a fund-by-fund portfolio list with commitment amounts was not confirmed.
rows.notes: Government fund-of-funds with £2.5bn to invest over 10 years from June 2018. Dated press releases can be part of the European LP proof set alongside EIF, KfW and Bpifrance.

rows.name: ESMA Registers (AIFMD, UCITS, EuVECA, EuSEF and ECSP entities; ELTIF register)
rows.licence: ESMA site terms (not checked)
rows.update_cadence: Continuous, driven by national competent authority (NCA) uploads
rows.coverage_estimate: ELTIF register: 159 ELTIFs (7 Mar 2025) [secondary]; 189 new ELTIFs authorised since start of 2024 from 72 new firms (2026) [secondary]; current AIFM, EuVECA and ECSP counts not retrieved, only 'a small number' of EuVECA managers registered; sub-threshold AIFMs (most small VC managers) are registered only nationally and not covered (as of 2026-10-25)
rows.limitations: No documented API; export as PDF or CSV only. Completeness depends on NCA uploads (patchy). Proves authorisation or registration status, not deployment, AUM or ticket. ELTIF and MMF are not in the entity interface (ELTIF register is a separate document, ESMA34-46-101). EUROCROWD flagged data-representation concerns in the ECSP register; withdrawn providers stay listed for five years.
rows.notes: Entity register filters: legal framework, name, home and host Member State, status, LEI, authorisation and withdrawal dates. Save CSV exports per legal framework. LEI links records to GLEIF.

rows.name: GLEIF LEI Golden Copy and Relationship Records
rows.licence: CC0; LEI Data Terms of Use forbid implying GLEIF endorsement or circumventing technical restrictions (liquidated damages CHF 100,000 per breach)
rows.update_cadence: Three times daily (02:00, 10:00, 18:00 UTC) with delta files against 8 h, 24 h, 7 days and 1 month
rows.coverage_estimate: Global LEI population (count not checked as of 2026-10-25); coverage of fund relationships depends on what LOUs and registrants report
rows.limitations: Identity only: no AUM, sector or deal data. Fund relationship coverage has gaps. API rate limit not found in official documentation (an unconfirmed '60 requests per minute' circulates). Filtering fund entities by EntityCategory 'FUND' unverified.
rows.notes: Identity spine for funds and managers. Relationship types IS_FUND-MANAGED_BY (fund to management entity), IS_SUBFUND_OF and IS_FEEDER_TO; pull managers via IS_FUND-MANAGED_BY end-nodes and group funds by manager LEI. Fund names often encode strategy and vintage. XML, CSV and JSON with geocodes and normalised addresses; API needs no authentication [secondary].

rows.name: EU national beneficial-ownership registers (after CJEU WM and Sovim)
rows.licence: GDPR-restricted; under AMLD6 (Directive (EU) 2024/1640) Art. 74 access only for authorities, obliged entities and persons demonstrating a legitimate interest
rows.limitations: Not usable for bulk commercial investor discovery. Public access ended after the CJEU ruling of 22 Nov 2022 (Art. 1(15)(c) AMLD5 invalid); Austria, the Netherlands, Belgium and Ireland suspended registers. AMLD6 register provisions were due 10 Jul 2026 and 18 Member States face infringement proceedings; Italy requires a documented 'direct, concrete and current' interest and its register remains suspended. No consolidated per-country status as of Oct 2026.
rows.notes: Recorded as evaluated and rejected. Url is a legal commentary (no single official entry point). National registers such as Slovakia's RPVS are catalogued separately.

rows.name: CalPERS Private Equity Program and Private Debt fund performance tables
rows.licence: Public records
rows.update_cadence: Semi-annual/quarterly with a ~2-quarter reporting lag (latest as of 31 Dec 2025)
rows.coverage_estimate: Active partnerships only, as of 31 Dec 2025 (program net IRR 11.6%, 1.5x); row count not captured
rows.limitations: Active funds only. No fund size or GP AUM (join to Form D and Form ADV by fund name). Table is a JavaScript web application that returned 'This Application Is Currently Unavailable' on 25 Oct 2026. Needs robust fund-name normalisation.
rows.notes: Columns: fund name, vintage year, capital committed, cash in, cash out, cash out plus remaining value, net IRR, investment multiple. Same format for Private Debt (e.g. Antares Credit Opportunities CA LLC, vintage 2021, $885m committed). Among the richest structured LP proof sources.

rows.name: Washington State Investment Board private equity reports and committee materials
rows.licence: Public records
rows.coverage_estimate: PE portfolio $49.9bn at 30 Jun 2025 [secondary]; fund count not captured
rows.limitations: PDF only; the example quarterly file found is from 2021 [pre-2024]; no fund size or GP AUM.
rows.notes: Quarterly 'Private Equity Portfolio Overview by Strategy' (IRRs computed by Hamilton Lane): corporate finance, growth equity, VC, special situations, distressed. Private markets committee materials name new commitments (e.g. Insight Partners XI $200m, Madison Dearborn VIII $250m, Nov 2025).

rows.name: European Investment Fund fund lists, InvestEU intermediaries and commitment press releases
rows.licence: EIF site terms (not checked)
rows.update_cadence: Ad hoc press releases; annual report
rows.coverage_estimate: 2024: 196 equity transactions, €7.2bn committed; Czechia: €334m to 17 VC/PE funds since 2002 (as of 15 May 2024); Slovakia 2025: guarantees plus €8m RRF, no new VC fund named; fund-list PDFs dated 30 Sep 2022
rows.limitations: Fund-list PDFs (active funds still investing; all active investments) date from 30 Sep 2022 [pre-2024] and exclude co-investments, business-angel deals and fund-of-funds structures; the VC & PE page returned 404 on 25 Oct 2026. The 17 Czech funds are not all named. No EIB-level fund list found.
rows.notes: InvestEU intermediary list is the most current EIF-wide roster. Per-deal press releases name fund and commitment (e.g. €30m to an Alfa Framtak fund). Czech EIF-backed managers named: Genesis Capital (first, 2002), Kaya, Credo, N1, Espira Investments; EIF money also helped create Lighthouse Ventures, i&i Biotech, Arx and Tilia Impact Ventures. Slovakia: €100m JEREMIE holding fund (2009) and three JEREMIE VC/seed funds (2014) [pre-2024]. EIF also runs the RRF fund of funds for Czech NPO start-up funds (see mpo-npo-vc-funds).

rows.name: KfW Capital reporting and press releases
rows.coverage_estimate: ~€2.9bn across 153 VC funds (end-2025); 2025 commitments ~€748m incl. €383m to 21 European VC funds; Growth Fund Germany ~€850m to 42 target funds; PitchBook's free view lists 38 commitments but shows 5 [paywalled]
rows.limitations: Aggregates and press releases only; no full fund-by-fund list with commitment sizes found.
rows.notes: KfW Capital portfolio sector split: ICT 47%, Life Sciences 21%, Industrial Tech 9%, Generalist 23%.

rows.name: Bpifrance fund-of-funds disclosures
rows.coverage_estimate: Retail fund-of-funds 'Bpifrance Entreprises 3' holds stakes in 76 French PE funds [secondary]
rows.limitations: No consolidated public partner-fund list found; aggregates only. No Bpifrance page itself is cited; url is a 2026 IPP report analysing Bpifrance private equity.

rows.name: Wikidata
rows.licence: CC0 (structured data)
rows.coverage_estimate: P1951 'investor': 7,190 statements, 980 distinct investors, 6,513 investees; direct P31 counts: VC firm 348, PE firm 90, PE fund 37, investment company 278 (SPARQL, 25 Oct 2026)
rows.limitations: Sparse (notable deals only; under 1,000 investors with P1951 edges), so not a primary source. Crowd-edited. Class counts exclude subclasses. Dated proof only where point-in-time (P585) qualifiers exist.
rows.notes: Use for seeding and cross-checking large, well-known investors; SPARQL with a polite User-Agent or weekly dumps. Related property P8324 'funder'. Items with industry (P452) = venture capital: 63; = private equity: 86.

rows.name: OpenCorporates
rows.licence: ODbL (share-alike, attribution) or a paid non-open licence; free access only for permitted users (personal use; journalists, NGOs and academics doing public-benefit research); financial institutions and corporations are not permitted users
rows.cost: API paid from £99/year; bulk free only if the derived database is shared under the open licence; free key reportedly 200 requests/month and 50/day [secondary, anecdotal]
rows.limitations: Treat as unavailable for a commercial product unless a licence is bought or ODbL share-alike is accepted for the derived database. Mirrors primary registries.
rows.notes: Use primary registers (Companies House, GLEIF, SEC, national registries) instead.

rows.name: Crunchbase free / Basic tier
rows.licence: Terms of Service (updated 30 Sep 2026) prohibit crawling or scraping, automated access or export, storing any significant portion and model training; Crunchbase Basic and the 2013 Snapshot are CC-BY but subject to the Terms
rows.cost: Free tier; API use or data export needs a separate arrangement
rows.coverage_estimate: No count in notes; vendor self-estimate of 85-95% accuracy for 2010-2012 VC rounds against VentureSource [pre-2024, vendor]
rows.limitations: Not reusable in bulk without a licence: the CC-BY carve-out is tied to ToS clauses that forbid scraping and storing significant portions. Do not ingest pages or the free tier. Commercial product is in the competitor table.
rows.notes: Data was historically CC-BY-NC / CC-BY until 2016 [pre-2024].

rows.name: Crunchbase 2013 Snapshot mirrors (Kaggle 'Startup Investments', GitHub)
rows.licence: CC-BY (Crunchbase 2013 Snapshot), subject to Crunchbase terms
rows.coverage_estimate: Data up to Dec 2013 [pre-2024]
rows.limitations: Stale; gives no evidence of current activity.

rows.name: OpenVC investor database
rows.licence: Terms of service not located; export only into the user's own CRM (CSV/XLS)
rows.coverage_estimate: 16,000+ early-stage investors claimed (one listing: 16,696 across 6,000+ firms, angel networks and family offices) (2026) [secondary]
rows.limitations: Self-reported stage, ticket and sector. Reuse terms unknown; review ToS before any use. OpenVC is also in the competitor table.

rows.name: Business Wire
rows.licence: Terms limit site use to submitting news releases, retrieving RSS feeds and reading releases
rows.limitations: Restrictive reuse terms: store only headline, URL, date and extracted facts (investor, investee, round, amount), not full text; review with counsel.
rows.notes: Press-release wires are the main open source of deal-level proof.

rows.name: GlobeNewswire
rows.licence: Terms not reviewed; media-partner arrangements offered
rows.update_cadence: Real-time (RSS feeds by subject, industry and exchange)
rows.limitations: Terms unverified; extract facts only.

rows.name: GDELT Project news index
rows.licence: Reportedly free for unlimited and unrestricted academic, commercial and governmental use with citation and link back [secondary; GDELT terms page not fetched]
rows.limitations: GDELT's own site and terms were not fetched; url is the secondary blog cited. Links out to original articles, whose own terms apply.
rows.notes: Most permissive news index; use as the discovery index linking out to original URLs, with fact extraction only.

rows.name: Common Crawl
rows.licence: No republishing of crawled content, no resale, no illegal use; users must respect crawled sites' terms
rows.limitations: Only its terms were evaluated; no use case for investor data was assessed.
rows.notes: Available through the AWS Open Data Registry.

rows.name: Investor firms' own websites, fund-close releases and annual reports
rows.licence: Site-specific; respect robots.txt and each site's terms
rows.coverage_estimate: No published measure of the share of firms stating ticket or fund size; combined with filings and deal news, at least ~80% of US/EU institutional VC/PE managers are estimated to have a verifiable footprint [estimate, unsourced] (as of 2026-10-25)
rows.limitations: Marketing claims that may be stale (e.g. old 'Fund II' pages); rate-limit, store URL and fetch date as proof, re-crawl periodically. 'Investable capital' rarely stated for large groups (proxy with balance-sheet equity). Single-family offices largely undocumented.
rows.notes: Only broad public source of stated ticket, sector and stage, often fund size. Url is an example (Penta Investments press release, 31 Mar 2026: group equity €5.6bn, 2025 net profit €714m); one site per investor. Large CZ/SK groups (Penta; likely J&T, PPF, KKCG) are verifiable via own releases and annual reports. LP lists in fund-close releases (e.g. Credo Fund V: RSJ, Marktlink, Willgrow) identify family offices acting as LPs.

rows.name: LinkedIn public profiles
rows.licence: User Agreement §8.2 (effective 3 Nov 2025) bans scraping or copying profiles and data, and bots or other automated access
rows.limitations: Contractually off-limits without a licence; scraping EU/UK natural persons' data also raises GDPR issues.
rows.notes: Recorded as evaluated and rejected (avoid without a licence).

rows.name: EBAN membership directory and Statistics Compendium
rows.update_cadence: Statistics compendium annual (2024 edition published Dec 2025)
rows.coverage_estimate: Over 100 member organisations (directory); ~47,610 active angels in networks and 359 networks across 39 countries in 2024 (339 elsewhere in the same document); 358 networks in 37 countries in 2023 [pre-2024]
rows.limitations: Organisation-level only; individual angels are not listed. Visible market only (EBAN dropped its 10x total-market multiplier).
rows.notes: Model angel networks as organisation records; add individual angels only with independent public proof and a GDPR basis.

rows.name: Angel Capital Association member directory
rows.cost: Public directory free; fuller directory members-only
rows.coverage_estimate: More than 15,000 individual investors (2022 overview) [pre-2024], against ~445,535 active US angels (2024 estimate); public directory lists angel groups, accredited platforms and affiliates
rows.limitations: Individual members are not listed for privacy reasons; current member counts not found.

rows.name: NBS Register of financial market entities (collective investment)
rows.licence: Not stated
rows.coverage_estimate: 368 management companies incl. foreign passported, 39 registered (sub-threshold) entities, 92 Slovak funds, 1,049 foreign funds, terminated 18 / 708 (accessed 2026-10-25)
rows.limitations: HTML only, no export visible ('Databáza na stiahnutie' content unverified). Registered managers are not supervised in depth and their AuM reports (Decree 1/2015) are not public. The 39 'registered entities' may include other entity types. No EuVECA mention.
rows.notes: Sub-threshold exemption (§31a(1) Act 203/2011): AuM up to €100m incl. leverage, or €500m unleveraged with no redemptions for 5 years. Registered managers must add 'manager of sub-threshold risk capital funds' to their business name by 30 Dec 2026, and NBS may remove managers by decision from 1 Jun 2026, so the list should become cleaner. Small enough to review by hand; closest Slovak equivalent of the Czech §15 list.

rows.name: Register právnických osôb (RPO)
rows.publisher: Štatistický úrad SR (Statistical Office of the Slovak Republic)
rows.licence: CC-BY 4.0 open government data per a third party [unverified]
rows.coverage_estimate: All Slovak legal persons, more than 1.4m entities [unverified, third party]
rows.limitations: Public version once described as informational and not legally binding (binding version restricted to state bodies) [pre-2024]. Rate limits not documented. SK NACE codes (64.30 / 64.99 / 66.30) are noisy: used by SPVs, family holdings and real-estate vehicles, while many VC managers sit under 70.22 or 66.30.
rows.notes: Gives name, legal form, status, address, share capital, activities, statutory bodies, shareholders ('stakeholders') and statistical codes. Combined with RÚZ, RPO shareholders can document holding-company portfolios. Also assigns IČO numbers.

rows.name: Register účtovných závierok (RÚZ) Open API
rows.licence: CC0
rows.update_cadence: Intraday (as soon as data appears on the web interface); per company about yearly
rows.coverage_estimate: All filers of financial statements (count not obtained as of 2026-10-25)
rows.limitations: Some filings have only public PDF attachments ('Verejné prílohy') or nothing public ('Neverejné'). Latest year typically 12-18 months behind. SK NACE filter is noisy. Rules changed from 1 Jun 2024 (Act 105/2024). No rate limits documented.
rows.notes: Strongest Slovak lever for AuM: fund vehicles (a.s., SICAV, s.r.o. GPs) file balance sheets whose financial-investment lines and equity proxy fund size. JSON v2.5 endpoints: /api/uctovne-jednotky, /api/uctovne-zavierky, /api/uctovne-vykazy, /api/vyrocne-spravy, templates /api/sablona(s), classifiers /api/sk-nace and /api/pravne-formy, PDF attachments. Incremental sync via zmenene-od, pokracovat-za-id, max-zaznamov (default 1,000, max 10,000); deleted records come back as stav ZMAZANÉ.

rows.name: Register partnerov verejného sektora (RPVS)
rows.publisher: Ministerstvo spravodlivosti SR (Ministry of Justice of the Slovak Republic)
rows.licence: Open Ownership BODS copy under Open Data Commons Attribution; ministry terms not stated
rows.coverage_estimate: Only firms contracting with the public sector (count not stated)
rows.limitations: Covers only public-sector partners; Open Ownership's BODS mappings are still 'in development'.
rows.notes: Act 315/2016, electronic only; holds public-sector partners, their beneficial owners (always natural persons) and the 'oprávnená osoba'. Ministry says data is also published in structured, machine-processable form. Gives UBO linkage for holding companies.

rows.name: Slovak Investment Holding (SIH): NDF II, Venture to Future Fund and intermediary pages
rows.licence: Not stated
rows.coverage_estimate: VFF: €40.4m (2019) + €15.3m RRP (May 2024), investing until end-2026; 2026-2030 tender for 3 start-up fund managers x €30m (€90m), deadline 30 Jun 2026, no award published as of 2026-10-25; social-economy funds €20.9m (2 x €10.45m)
rows.limitations: Intermediary pages omit SIH commitment amounts. Legacy funds (Vision Ventures, Neulogy Ventures, Limerock) are past their investment period. Tender outcome not yet published. SIH group AuM of €1,593m (end-2025) unverified.
rows.notes: SIH is 100% owned by SZRB; subsidiary Slovak Asset Management is fund manager of NDF II. VFF tickets €400k-€7m, always pari passu with private co-investors; EIB signed a €10m equity commitment (20 Dec 2019). TED notice 167128-2026: the award notice will name 3 new active Slovak VC managers. €15m for seed-stage companies from the RRP (June 2024). Social-economy funds managed by CB ESPRI and Sociálni Inovátori Impact Capital.

rows.name: SLOVCA member lists
rows.publisher: Slovak Venture Capital and Private Equity Association (SLOVCA)
rows.licence: Not stated
rows.coverage_estimate: 12 full members and 31 associate members, of which only ~3 associates look like investors (accessed 2026-10-25)
rows.limitations: Self-selected; mixes PE houses, VC and public bodies; associates are mostly law, audit, insurance and bank firms. Member profiles are on slovca.sk only, with no external URLs. The 'Štatistiky' section shows no figures.
rows.notes: Full members: ARX Equity Partners, CVI, Enterprise Investors, Eterus Capital, Fond inovácií a technológií, Genesis Capital, Jet Investment, Národný holdingový fond, Neulogy Ventures, Sandberg Capital, Venture to Future Fund, Vision Ventures. Investor-like associates: Across Private Investments, G4 Investments, Slovak Investment Holding. Founded 1995 in Bratislava; IČO 31 748 341.

rows.name: Klub podnikateľských anjelov Slovenska (Slovak business angel network)
rows.coverage_estimate: Founded 2011 by ZMPS and the Slovak Business Agency [pre-2024]; 'Slovak Business Angels' listed with tickets of €10k-€80k (2020) [pre-2024]; current members not found
rows.limitations: Only pre-2024 mentions; no own website or member list captured (url is a news topic page). SBAN member list not retrieved. EBAN's 2016 CEE community does not show a current Slovak EBAN member.

rows.name: Startup Report Slovensko 2025
rows.coverage_estimate: Survey of 600 firms and investors; 183 start-ups and 41 investors responded (2025)
rows.limitations: Known only via news coverage (url is the news article); report itself not opened; in Slovak.

rows.name: ČNB JERRS lists of regulated and registered entities (incl. §15 ZISIF list) and WS JERRS
rows.licence: ČNB site terms (not confirmed)
rows.cost: Free web lists; WS JERRS needs a commercial certificate (eIdentity, I.CA, PostSignum or an EU-trusted issuer) and a signed registration request
rows.update_cadence: Daily publication (last 24 Oct 2026 01:45:50); status dates back to 1 Jan 2009
rows.coverage_estimate: Full regulated universe since 2009, incl. funds, AIFMs and §15 sub-threshold managers; counts not retrieved; qualified-investor funds (FKI) reportedly 516 (end-2024) to 585 (end-2025) [unverified]
rows.limitations: §15 entries are notifications, not licences, and are not supervised (annual asset report only to confirm the €100m ceiling); many are real-estate or club-deal vehicles, so the pool is noisy; ČNB warns a listing is not an endorsement. Contact details updated only when entities notify. Machine access needs a certificate.
rows.notes: Menus: Přímé vyhledání, Základní seznamy (the §15 list is the last item), Počty subjektů (counts at a date and time series; pull for 2026-10-25 before the pilot), Vznik a zánik subjektů. Each entity has a 'vizitka'. WS JERRS (since 1 Jul 2019): https://aplc.cnb.cz/jerrsws/ws, SOAP/XML with WSDL/XSD, operations getSubjekt, getSubjekty, getZastoupeny; request to jerrsws@cnb.cz.

rows.name: ARES (Administrativní registr ekonomických subjektů)
rows.publisher: Ministerstvo financí ČR (Ministry of Finance of the Czech Republic)
rows.licence: Not confirmed
rows.coverage_estimate: All Czech economic subjects (aggregated from registers)
rows.limitations: Aggregator of other registers; endpoint details come from third-party clients and should be checked against the official Katalog veřejných služeb PDF (v08, 2023-08-01). Licence and rate limits not documented in what was read.
rows.notes: REST: POST https://ares.gov.cz/ekonomicke-subjekty-v-be/rest/ekonomicke-subjekty/vyhledat for search, GET /ekonomicke-subjekty/{ico} for lookup by IČO.

rows.name: ČSÚ Registr ekonomických subjektů (RES) open data
rows.licence: Not confirmed
rows.update_cadence: Twice a month (as at the 15th and month-end)
rows.coverage_estimate: All Czech economic subjects (count not stated)
rows.limitations: CZ-NACE is a noisy investor filter (seed list only, never proof). Dual coding: CZ-NACE 2025 exports from 1 Jan 2026, old codes until 31 Dec 2028. Licence not confirmed.
rows.notes: Files res_data.csv (IČO, name, address, legal form, creation and dissolution dates) and res_pf_nace.csv (legal forms and NACE activities), UTF-8 CSV with JSON metadata schemas.

rows.name: Veřejný rejstřík open data (dataor.justice.cz)
rows.licence: Not confirmed
rows.update_cadence: Daily for the current year [third party, unverified]
rows.coverage_estimate: All entities in the Czech public registers
rows.limitations: Very large files; streaming XML parsing recommended. Beneficial-owner register reportedly closed to the public since 17 Dec 2025 [unverified, single non-official source]. Financial statements sit in the Sbírka listin as scanned or PDF documents, not structured data [not verified], so AuM extraction is costlier than with Slovakia's RÚZ.
rows.notes: CSV and XML exports of register extracts (officers, shareholders, etc.). Shareholder records can document holding-company and family-office portfolios.

rows.name: Národní rozvojová banka (NRB) / Národní rozvojová investiční (NRI) fund programmes
rows.licence: Not stated
rows.coverage_estimate: NRI 'Fond Ukrajina': one manager selected (DEPO Ventures One SCSp), CZK 94m committed, up to CZK 141m with private money (date not captured)
rows.limitations: Only press coverage on BusinessInfo found (url is that article; no NRB page cited); no consolidated fund list; article dates not captured. The separate Czech 'Národní rozvojový fond' invests in infrastructure, not VC [pre-2024].
rows.notes: NRI is 100% owned by NRB and is its equity / fund-of-funds arm. Fond Ukrajina targets start-ups from Ukraine, Moldova and Georgia.

rows.name: MPO / Národní plán obnovy start-up funds via the EIF RRF fund of funds
rows.publisher: Ministerstvo průmyslu a obchodu ČR (MPO) with the EIF
rows.licence: Not stated
rows.coverage_estimate: 3 pilot NPO start-up funds planned with the EIF, ~CZK 1.3bn (other articles say CZK 3.3bn); first: Tensor Ventures Co-investment Fund, up to €50m incl. up to €20m NPO money (2024)
rows.limitations: Press coverage only; programme size figures conflict; managers beyond Tensor Ventures not named in the notes.
rows.notes: Tensor fund invests in pre-seed digital start-ups (~50 over 5 years), always co-investing with other VCs. MPO is responsible for the NPO money channelled through the EIF RRF fund of funds.

rows.name: Czech Business Angel Association (CBAA)

Runs a free angel-investing course with ESIL and LUMUS Investment. World Bank (2018) found Czech angel investing small, Prague- and ICT-concentrated, with little syndication [pre-2024].

rows.name: CzechCrunch (news, Startupové Česko, CC+)
rows.licence: Proprietary
rows.cost: Free articles; CC+ paywall for investor rankings and the 100+ investor database
rows.coverage_estimate: 75 announced rounds by Czech founders in 2025, CZK 9.8bn total, median round CZK 29m (2 Jan 2026); Startupové Česko 2025 headline CZK 13.33bn (-19.78%); investor database of 100+ investors paywalled
rows.limitations: Most-active-funds chart and investor database behind the CC+ paywall. Totals differ from other trackers because methodologies differ.

rows.name: Forbes Česko
rows.limitations: Article dates often not captured; the annual round-up ('Investoři při chuti…') returned only its headline. AuM figures are self-reported or promotional (e.g. One Family Office ~CZK 12bn).
rows.notes: Cited for MPO/NPO start-up funds, CBAA, One Family Office (Havel & Partners) and the Smart Market Report figures.

rows.name: Ambit VC Deals Report 2025
rows.coverage_estimate: ~100 Czech VC deals in 2025 vs up to 200 a year in 2021-22; median early-stage ticket €500k, median pre-money €6.5m, more than 80% early stage
rows.limitations: Figures from a search snippet (the BusinessInfo page returned 403); report itself not opened.
rows.notes: Benchmark for the size of the Czech pilot universe and ticket sanity checks.

rows.name: Smart Market Report (Czech start-up investment)
rows.coverage_estimate: Investment in Czech start-ups up 174% to CZK 14.3bn in 2024
rows.limitations: Known only via Forbes CZ coverage (url is that article); methodology differs from CzechCrunch and Invest Europe.

rows.name: Invest Europe Central and Eastern Europe Private Equity Statistics
rows.licence: Invest Europe copyright
rows.coverage_estimate: EDC-covered funds, market approach, 17 CEE countries; 2011-2025: 30 Czech-based and 8 Slovak-based funds raised capital (€1,958.2m vs €252.8m); 2025 investment CZ ~€275.3m (0.080% of GDP), SK ~€7m in 5 companies (0.005%)
rows.limitations: Badly under-counts VC in CZ and SK compared with Dealroom and CzechCrunch (market approach by portfolio-company HQ, EDC survey coverage, diaspora start-ups abroad). PDF tables have garbled layout. Aggregates only: use for cross-country ratios and fund counts, not as a deal census.
rows.notes: Cleanest public, comparable proxy for the number of locally based PE/VC fund vehicles (CZ:SK about 4:1). 2024: family offices and private individuals were 21% of CEE fundraising. Slovak press (Startitup) relays these figures.
